mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from t-1w to t-0w signals more in-person commuting, which raises weekday retail visits with a lag and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays near or above its t-0w level but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT below its recent week-average indicates weaker public-transport access to shopping corridors, which depresses discretionary retail trips within one to two weeks and pushes RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -12 for a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is negative in all four weeks and reaches -11.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains at or below -12 weekly yet RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES weaken at the same time, commuting-linked footfall shrinks and retail demand softens over the following month; the combined drop matters more than either series alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both series are below or near baseline and show week-to-week volatility
failure_condition: If simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is followed by a higher 28-day mean RETAIL_REC than the prior 28 days, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above its recent range, households are spending more time near home, which substitutes away from discretionary shopping trips and lowers RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is elevated at 6.3, 6.0, 8.0, and 7.1 across the four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 and RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility captures leisure substitution toward outdoor activities, which diverts discretionary spending from malls and entertainment venues and reduces RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS becomes more negative from -35.1 to -43.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS improves materially but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 28 days, the substitution mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated while RETAIL_REC stays depressed, households are reallocating trips toward necessity shopping and away from discretionary retail, causing RETAIL_REC to stay lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 8 while RETAIL_REC remains below -15
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated but RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks, the necessity-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized fall in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below their recent means indicates tighter movement constraints or reduced commuting opportunities, which suppresses retail foot traffic and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their 2-week means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is negative and WORKPLACES turns from 0.0 to 2.3 after -8.0
failure_condition: If both commuting proxies fall below their recent means but RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in PARKS combined with stable or rising GROCERY_PHARM indicates households are staying home and making short local trips instead of discretionary outings, which keeps RETAIL_REC below its previous four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to fall while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.
